name: Render
description: Render is a cloud platform for deploying and scaling web services, static sites, background workers, cron jobs, private services, and databases, positioned as "the cloud for builders."
best_for: Developers and teams migrating from Heroku, Railway, or Fly.io, plus startups and builders who want straightforward deployment with minimal infrastructure management.
features: Autoscaling that automatically adjusts resources based on demand
Private networking for secure communication between services
Persistent disks for durable application storage
Infrastructure as Code for defining and managing infrastructure programmatically
Preview environments for testing changes before production
Render API, CLI, and MCP integration for agent-driven workflows

alternatives.name: Vercel
alternatives.description: Agentic infrastructure for deploying web apps and AI agents at global scale with Git-connected preview deploys.
alternatives.best_for: Developers and platform builders deploying apps and autonomous agent workflows.

alternatives.name: Netlify
alternatives.description: A platform to create with AI or code and deploy instantly on production infrastructure.
alternatives.best_for: Product engineers and teams building and deploying web apps.

alternatives.name: Supabase
alternatives.description: An open source Firebase alternative providing a Postgres-backed backend with auth, storage, and edge functions.
alternatives.best_for: Developers who want a managed backend built on Postgres.

tiers.name: Hobby (workspace plan)
tiers.notes: Free workspace plan for individuals/prototypes. Limited to 1 team seat, 1 workspace, max 25 services, 2 environments per project, 5GB bandwidth included (then $0.15/GB), 500 build pipeline minutes (then $5/1,000 min), 7-day log retention. Compute for actual services is billed separately (free compute tier available with limits, or paid compute starting at $7/month).

tiers.name: Starter compute instance (smallest paid compute plan)
tiers.unit: per service, prorated to the second
tiers.notes: Cheapest paid resource on Render: <1 CPU / 512MB RAM web service or worker. This is billed on top of a workspace plan (even the free Hobby plan) — it is the actual lowest dollar amount a paying Render customer can spend, distinct from the platform's own subscription tiers.

tiers.name: Pro (workspace plan)
tiers.unit: flat rate, unlimited team members (no per-seat fee)
tiers.notes: For teams deploying production apps. Unlimited team members, unlimited services/projects/environments, SOC 2 + ISO 27001 reports, audit logs, full-stack preview environments. As of an April 23, 2026 pricing change, this replaced the old 'Professional' per-seat plan which charged $19/member/month.

tiers.name: Scale (workspace plan)
tiers.unit: flat rate, unlimited team members (no per-seat fee)
tiers.notes: Adds SAML SSO, SCIM, advanced RBAC, HIPAA-eligible workspaces, multi-workspace organization management. Replaced the old 'Organization' per-seat plan which charged $29/member/month.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.notes: Custom pricing; contractual SLAs, dedicated support, dedicated technical account manager, support response SLAs. No public numbers. Billing basis: custom.

cons: Render's free tier is not viable for anything long-running or persistent: free web services spin down after 15 minutes without inbound traffic and take about a minute to wake back up on the next request, and free Postgres databases hard-expire 30 days after creation (with only a 14-day grace period to upgrade before the data is lost) — confirmed on Render's own docs page at render.com/docs/free. Free Key Value (Redis) instances are in-memory only and lose all data on every restart.

Enterprise-grade governance and compliance features -- SAML SSO, SCIM, HIPAA BAA, advanced RBAC, and multi-workspace organization management -- are gated entirely behind the Scale plan at a flat $499/month, a roughly 20x jump from the Pro plan's $25/month with no intermediate tier offering SSO alone. This is a real structural cliff for a mid-sized team that needs single sign-on but not full HIPAA/multi-workspace governance, per render.com/pricing and render.com/docs/new-workspace-plans.

Even the paid flat-rate plans meter and surcharge core usage on top of the subscription: Hobby and Pro include only 5GB of bandwidth/month before $0.15/GB overage charges, 500 build-pipeline minutes/month before $5 per additional 1,000 minutes, and just 2 custom domains before $0.25/domain/month. Render's own changelog (render.com/changelog/updated-plans-for-render-workspaces) explicitly notes the new flat-rate Hobby and Pro plans include *reduced* bandwidth compared to the legacy per-seat plans they replaced, so the simplified sticker price can still mean a lower included quota than before.
